newsitem.title: UK: Small UK firms see brighter future-3i survey.
newsitem.headline: Small UK firms see brighter future-3i survey.

text.p: For the first time since January 1994, small- and medium-sized UK companies are becoming more optimistic both about their own outlook and about the UK economy, a business survey said on Monday.

The 3i Enterprise Barometer Index, which provides a survey of confidence among venture capital backed companies in the UK, stands at "plus 70," having risen from "plus 44" in the last quarter and just "plus 17" in October 1995, the group said.

The companies surveyed -- backed by investment fund 3i -- reported a rise in expansion prospects from a balance of "plus 20 percent" in May this year to "plus 35 percent" now, it added in a statement.
More companies also believe that the economic climate is now right to start a new business.
"Moreover, they are also noticeably more optimistic about their own sales and profitability for the current quarter than they were in the previous survey," it added.
"This is underpinned by an equally bullish forecast for increased investment."

More companies in southern England and in the non- manufacturing sector continue to expect to raise employment that manufacturing companies in the north. But confidence among northern firms had improved "considerably," the survey added. The 3i Enterprise Barometer is drawn every quarter from responses from a random sample of 1,000 companies in which the fund has an investment. The response rate for this survey -- carried out between July 19 and August 17 -- was 49.3 percent.
